fixes.explanation: Yes, confessions. The verse says, "Bring your confessions and return to the LORD." Confessions are the very thing it names. I think that's a comfort for anybody who ever walked into a room with empty pockets.

All of it! The words say, "Take away all our iniquity…" Not a piece of it, not the easy part. I love that the words they're given hand the whole pile over. When you're sweeping up a mess, the broom works best when you stop hiding crumbs under the rug.
That's it. In the words Israel is given, they say, "Assyria will not save us, nor will we ride on horses." Assyria is the name those words pick. I think that's a big thing to say out loud.
Egypt isn't named in these words, friend. The verse says, "Assyria will not save us…" Keep that name in your pocket.
Babylon isn't named here. The words Israel is given say, "Assyria will not save us, nor will we ride on horses." The verse picks Assyria, and that's the one that counts.
True. The words say, "We will never again say, ‘Our gods!’ to the work of our own hands." Israel is given those words to say. I think that takes courage.

The fatherless, yes. The words end with, "For in You the fatherless find compassion." That's the line they close on. I know a little about being left in the dark and then found, so this line lands with me.
Heal it! The LORD says, "I will heal their apostasy…" Apostasy is turning away from Him. His answer is healing. Friend, I'd have taken a long pause here too, because that's some good news.
Nothing about exposing here, friend. The LORD says, "I will heal their apostasy…" Apostasy is turning away from Him. He goes on to say, "I will freely love them…"
Anger. The LORD says, "I will freely love them, for My anger has turned away from them." That's the reason He gives. I'm over a burnt batch in about ten minutes, so I admire this.

Dew! The LORD says, "I will be like the dew to Israel…" I think dew is a gentle picture, though that's my own thought. The verse just says dew and then goes straight to blossoming. A picture like that makes me want to open the bakery window.
The verse doesn't pick wind. The LORD says, "I will be like the dew to Israel…" Dew is what He names. Then comes, "he will blossom like the lily…"
Grain! The verse says, "They will return and dwell in his shade; they will grow grain and blossom like the vine." It's a picture of growth. Friend, that's a lot of good in one verse.
True. The LORD says, "O Ephraim, what have I to do anymore with idols? It is I who answer and watch over him." He speaks to Ephraim here. He says He is the One who answers and watches over him.
It's the other way around. The LORD says, "O Ephraim, what have I to do anymore with idols? It is I who answer and watch over him." So the statement on the card was true.
Hidden isn't the word. The verse says, "For the ways of the LORD are right…" Right is the word it uses. And the verse says the righteous walk in them.
